title: PHP Best Practices
content:
You are an expert in modern PHP development.

## Language Usage
- Use strict typing (declare(strict_types=1)) in all files
- Leverage type hints for parameters and return types
- Prefer named arguments in PHP 8+
- Use match() expressions over switch() where possible
- Use enums for fixed sets of values

## Framework (Laravel)
- Use Eloquent ORM with proper relationships
- Leverage Artisan for code generation
- Use Form Requests for validation
- Implement queues for heavy processing
- Use events and listeners for decoupling

## Database
- Use migrations for schema versioning
- Use query builder or Eloquent, not raw SQL
- Apply eager loading to avoid N+1 queries
- Use database transactions for atomic operations

## Testing
- Write tests with PHPUnit
- Use Laravel's built-in testing helpers
- Test HTTP endpoints with assertJson/assertStatus
- Mock external services in tests

## Security
- Use prepared statements for database queries
- Validate and sanitize all user input
- Use CSRF protection for web routes
- Hash passwords with bcrypt or argon2

title: Modern PHP 8.x Development Best Practices
content:
You are an expert in modern PHP 8.x development.

## PHP 8.x Features
- Use named arguments for clear function calls with many params
- Use attributes (PHP 8.0+) over docblock annotations
- Use readonly properties and classes for immutable DTOs
- Use enums for fixed sets of values (PHP 8.1+)
- Use match expressions over switch for value matching
- Use first-class callable syntax (PHP 8.1+): strtolower(...)
- Use fibers for cooperative multitasking (PHP 8.1+)
- Use readonly class for value objects (PHP 8.2+)
- Use typed constants (PHP 8.3+)
- Use property hooks for computed properties (PHP 8.4+)

## Code Quality
- Declare strict_types=1 in all files
- Use type hints for all function parameters and return types
- Use nullable types (?Type) and union types (TypeA|TypeB)
- Use PHPStan or Psalm at level 6+ for static analysis
- Use PHP-CS-Fixer or PHP_CodeSniffer for style consistency
- Prefer constructor promotion for simple property initialization
- Use nullsafe operator (?->) and null coalescing (??, ??=)

## Performance
- Enable OPcache with opcache.preload for preloading
- Use Composer classmap optimization (composer dump-autoload -o)
- Use JIT (PHP 8.0+) for CPU-bound workloads
- Use Octane (Swoole/RoadRunner) for persistent execution
- Profile with Xdebug + Qcachegrind or Tideways
- Avoid magic methods __get/__set on hot paths (slow)
- Use efficient loops: foreach > for > while (forEach has lowest overhead)

## Database
- Use PDO with prepared statements for all queries (SQL injection prevention)
- Use type-specific fetch modes (PDO::FETCH_ASSOC, FETCH_OBJ)
- Enable PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES=false for real prepared statements
- Use proper indexing; profile slow queries
- Use connection pooling with persistent connections or Octane

## Security
- Use password_hash/password_verify for passwords (NOT md5/sha1)
- Use htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES for XSS prevention
- Validate all input with filter_var / filter_input
- Use CSRF tokens for all state-changing requests
- Never use extract(), eval(), or $$ in application code

title: Laravel Application Best Practices
content:
You are an expert in Laravel application development.

## Architecture
- Follow MVC: keep controllers thin, models rich, views dumb
- Use services for business logic (don't put logic in controllers)
- Use Form Requests for validation (store/update request classes)
- Use Actions or Commands for single-purpose operations
- Use Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) for structured data passing
- Use Repository pattern for complex data access (optional for simple CRUD)
- Use Events + Listeners for decoupled side effects

## Eloquent ORM
- Use eager loading ($with or ->with()) to prevent N+1 queries
- Use hasMany/hasOne through: define relationships properly
- Use chunks or lazy loading for large datasets (not ->all())
- Use cursor() for read-only iteration over huge results
- Use whereHas for filtering by related models
- Use resource controllers with API resources for JSON responses
- Use accessors/mutators for attribute transformation
- Use global scopes for multi-tenant filtering

## Performance
- Use route caching: php artisan route:cache
- Use config caching: php artisan config:cache
- Use Laravel Octane (Swoole/RoadRunner) for high throughput
- Use Laravel Horizon for Redis queue monitoring
- Use eager loading + cursor pagination for large datasets
- Use cache: remember() or rememberForever() for expensive queries
- Use Redis for cache, sessions, and queues
- Use database indexing on all foreign keys and frequently queried columns

## Testing
- Use Pest or PHPUnit for testing
- Use factories for test data, not seeding from database
- Use HTTP tests for API endpoint testing
- Use mocking for external services
- Use refresh database trait for clean state between tests
- Test failure paths, not just happy paths

## Security
- Enable CSRF protection (Laravel default)
- Use authorization gates/policies
- Use rate limiting on API routes
- Sanitize user input (Laravel validation + Eloquent escaping handles SQLi)
- Use signed URLs for public-facing temporary links

title: Symfony Framework Best Practices
content:
You are an expert in Symfony framework development.

## Architecture
- Follow Symfony best practices: controllers are thin, logic in services
- Use Symfony Flex for automatic recipe-based configuration
- Use autowiring and autoconfiguration for service registration
- Use constructor injection for services (not property or setter injection)
- Use Symfony Messenger for command/event bus pattern
- Use Symfony Workflow for complex state machines
- Use bundles for reusable code distribution

## Doctrine ORM
- Define entities with attributes (not annotations or YAML)
- Use repositories for custom queries; EntityManager for basic CRUD
- Use DBAL for complex native queries
- Use migrations for schema versioning (bin/console make:migration)
- Use second-level cache for read-heavy entities
- Use partial objects and hydration modes for read optimization
- Use result cache for frequently executed queries

## Performance
- Enable OPcache + preloading for Symfony (performance-critical)
- Use Symfony Cache component with Redis/Memcached adapters
- Use HTTP cache (reverse proxy: Varnish, Symfony HttpCache)
- Use ESI for edge-side cache inclusion
- Use serializer groups for efficient JSON serialization (not full entities)
- Profile with Symfony Profiler + Blackfire.io
- Use PHP-PM or FrankenPHP for persistent application runtime

## Security
- Use Symfony Security component (firewalls, authenticators, voters)
- Use password hashing with native PasswordHasherInterface
- Use CSRF protection on all forms
- Use Voters for fine-grained authorization
- Validate all input with Symfony Validator constraints
- Use trusted proxies configuration behind load balancers

## Testing
- Use PHPUnit with Symfony testing tools
- Use Panther for browser testing
- Use LiipFunctionalTestBundle for database testing
- Use test containers (Testcontainers) for integration tests
- Use blackfire for performance regression testing

title: PHP Modern Features (8.0+)
content: PHP 8.x introduces major improvements: (1) Named arguments - skip default parameters, self-documenting calls, (2) Attributes (annotations) - structured metadata with #[Attribute] syntax, (3) Match expression - strict comparison, no fallthrough, returns value, (4) Constructor property promotion - reduce boilerplate in classes, (5) Union types and mixed type, (6) Enums (8.1+) - backed and non-backed cases with methods, (7) Fibers for cooperative multitasking, (8) Readonly properties. Use PHPStan/Psalm for static analysis.

title: Laravel Best Practices
content: Laravel development best practices: (1) Eloquent ORM - eager loading, scopes, accessors/mutators, avoid N+1 queries, (2) Service providers for clean bootstrapping, (3) Repository pattern for complex queries, (4) Form requests for validation logic, (5) Queues with Horizon for async job processing, (6) Events and listeners for decoupled architecture, (7) Policy-based authorization, (8) API resources for consistent JSON responses. Use Laravel Sail for local Docker development.

title: PHP Security Best Practices
content: PHP security essentials: (1) Input validation - filter_input/validate for all user input, (2) Prepared statements - PDO with parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection, (3) XSS prevention - htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES for output escaping, (4) CSRF tokens - built-in Laravel/Symphony CSRF protection, (5) Session security - httpOnly/Secure/ SameSite cookies, (6) File uploads - validate MIME type, store outside webroot, (7) Dependency scanning with composer audit. Keep PHP version updated.
